attractions.name: Pacco Qillo (Hyderabad Fort)
attractions.description: A historic fort built by the Talpur rulers, offering views over the old city and Indus River plains.

attractions.name: Sindh Museum
attractions.description: A museum showcasing Sindh's cultural and archaeological heritage, including Indus Valley artifacts.

attractions.name: Tombs of the Talpur Mirs
attractions.description: Elaborately decorated royal tombs of the Talpur dynasty, showcasing intricate tile-work.

attractions.name: Resham Gali & Shahi Bazaar
attractions.description: Traditional markets famous for Sindhi textiles, bangles, and handicrafts.

weather_info.climate_type: Hot desert climate, very hot summers with mild winters

travel_tips.tip: Use the Hyderabad Bypass to avoid the busy city center when passing through en route between Karachi and upper Sindh.
Ride-hailing apps work well for reaching the fort and old city markets.
Stay hydrated and avoid extended outdoor sightseeing during peak summer afternoon heat.
Visit Shahi Bazaar and the old city in the morning or early evening to avoid the midday heat.

history.founded: Founded in 1768 by Mian Ghulam Shah Kalhoro
history.city_history: Hyderabad served as the capital of Sindh under both the Kalhora and Talpur dynasties before British annexation in 1843, after which the capital shifted to Karachi. It remains one of Sindh's major cultural and educational centers, known for its historic forts, bazaars, and Talpur-era architecture.
history.province_history: Sindh is home to one of the world's oldest urban civilizations, the Indus Valley Civilization (Mohenjo-daro), and was later ruled by Persian, Arab, and Mughal empires, as well as the Talpur dynasty, before British annexation in 1843 and eventual inclusion in Pakistan in 1947.
